book.title: The account in one page
book.text:
Rafferty Holdings is a family-owned financial services group led by Michael Rafferty. Its businesses include Direxion, a large ETF provider, Hilton Capital Management, a real estate arm, a capital markets arm, and Rafferty Ventures, which invests the family's money deal by deal. Supernal has two contracts with the group, both starting 29 Jul 2026. Rafferty Ventures pays $10,000 a month for Ventures OS, a working application with an AI coworker named Argus. Rafferty Holdings pays $5,000 a month for a Chief AI Officer service, which today means discovery sessions, training and advice. Together that is $180,000 a year.

The account is more important than its size. Michael has put about $4M into Infinity, the company that trades as Supernal, so the client is also an owner. The original hope was a relationship worth over $1M across four or five entities. Two further builds were prepared, a personal asset dashboard for Michael and an ad production tool for Direxion. Neither was signed. In October Rafferty chose to hire its own AI engineers and paused new builds.

Both accounts now sit in the “watch” band, at 3.4 and 3.2 out of 5. Ventures has a product people like but do not yet use daily. Holdings has recovered from a low of 2.0 because Shari James, the CFO, asked Supernal to train the firm and help it hire. Katie Jefferson leads both day to day, with Thomas Bustos as the named Chief AI Officer, Felipe Orlando as the one engineer, and Johnny Borbone as account lead.

book.title: Why they bought
book.text:
Jack Grady runs the daily work of Rafferty Ventures with Henry Mulholland above him and two associates beside him. In May he described a week with about 24 hours of meetings, an inbox used as a to-do list, files sorted by hand into dated folders, and call prep done by typing prompts into Claude. The team is small and will stay small, so their stated problem was keeping everything in one place: who said what, what was promised, which portfolio company had gone quiet, which introduction was owed.

Supernal answered with a prototype built in two weeks on invented data. Jack asked for almost nothing to change. Three things he said shaped the product: a drafted reply that is 80% right is already a big saving; he wants to see what the AI did; and the tool should become his main channel, not another place to look. Price was shown only after the demo, on purpose. Client ownership of the code, a flat fee with usage absorbed, and a promise of continuous building rather than maintenance closed it.

The holding company bought for different reasons. It was rolling out Claude Enterprise and saw AI as a change in how the firm works. The finance team wanted a faster close. Leaders wanted help choosing what to do first. Supernal priced the Chief AI Officer seat at $5,000, a third of its usual rate, to hold the coordinating role across every entity. The investor tie made Supernal the natural first call.

book.title: How the deal is built
book.text:
There are five pieces and only two are signed. The Ventures order form commits Supernal to four milestones in 90 days, then monthly cycles at the same fee, with a backlog for a second phase. The client can leave at the end of month 6 if it gives notice around the end of month 5, which falls in late December 2026. The Holdings order form is a strategy contract: discovery, a roadmap, a mid-year review and a monthly leadership review. It says plainly that any build needs a separate order form, and that the Chief AI Officer supervises builds across the group.

That design made the Holdings contract the trunk and each build a branch. Ventures was the first branch. Holdings OS, the dashboard for Michael with the AI analyst Atlas, was to be the second, first at $13,500 a month with Atlas, then at $7,500 without. Direxion's ad tool was to be the third at $10,000. Each was meant to have its own pod.

Three things link the pieces in daily life. Shari James signs for all of them. SMPL Technologies, the outside IT firm, controls every permission for all of them. And the Ventures team's monthly deck, now produced by Ventures OS, is how Michael sees that branch.

The paperwork has loose ends: both signed forms are numbered OF-001, one carries another client's name in the signature block, and the unsigned Holdings OS draft has an inconsistent fee line and eight open legal questions.

book.title: Michael's Life App and the price problem
book.text:
The Holdings OS prototype was the most impressive thing Supernal showed Rafferty and the deal that did the most damage. It put Michael's whole financial world on one screen, with Atlas giving a daily brief and answering questions by text or voice. Shari and Jackie Bader saw it in July and said the group was ready. Michael saw it on 20 Aug. He liked the idea of asking about a deal from a dinner table, but said he was unsure how much he would use the interactive part.

Price was the real trouble. Supernal's own estimate of running costs was under $7,000 a month, and comparable clients pay $30,000 to $90,000. Johnny wanted $13,500; Tauseef thought $10,000 was the most the scope could bear. Before the pitch, Brennan had told Michael it could be done for $150,000 up front and $1,500 a month. Michael's view was that he had already invested millions and should not pay again for the people. Johnny had to walk the quote back in a private conversation. The team then split the deal: $7,500 a month for the platform, Atlas later. The internal review scored margin at 2 out of 5 and accepted it for the relationship.

No scoping call on real data sources was ever held, and there was no clear way to connect bank accounts. By mid September Michael had found a cheaper vendor through a contact and the deal was paused. The team later judged that Rafferty felt misled twice on price.
sources: Life App & Overall Supernal AI Update, 20 Aug 2026

book.title: Ventures OS and why it is built this way
book.text:
Ventures OS does not replace Affinity, the CRM the team uses all day. It mirrors Affinity on a schedule and adds what Affinity lacks: the three partners' calendars, their deal-related email, the files in the Investments SharePoint site, and call transcripts. From that it builds a page per deal, laid out for the deal's stage, with a brief for the next call, the tasks each side owes, research on the company, and alerts when things go quiet. It also produces the monthly deck for Michael.

Several choices explain its shape. Affinity released its own AI features a week after kickoff, so a plain dashboard would have been redundant. Tauseef argued for a conversational coworker instead, and Argus was built on the Hermes framework so that it could remember, monitor and take instructions. Argus is told never to fill a gap: if a tool returns nothing, it says what it checked. The five stages and their triggers came from a long question-and-answer session with Jack, after early briefs proved to be lists of one-liners. Transcripts are visible only to people who were on the invite, because Henry's conversations can be sensitive. Email is read only for deal domains and shown as highlights, which is what SMPL would approve. GP View, the old portfolio reporting tool, was dropped because nobody answered its emails.

The latest lesson came on 4 Nov. A rule that guessed a transcript's company from nearby calendar entries was wrong every time. It was switched off. Showing “no deal” is safer than showing the wrong deal.
sources: AI Coworker for Rafferty Ventures, 27 Aug 2026

book.title: How delivery has gone
book.text:
Milestone 1 closed on time in mid August with Affinity connected and environments live. After that the plan met SMPL. Access to Outlook, calendar and SharePoint, expected in week 2, took until late September and October. SMPL's concerns were reasonable: mailbox permissions allow impersonation, and automated filing removes the moment when a person would notice a bad attachment. They sent 13 written questions; the answers took a week to polish. The folder Jack called OneDrive turned out to be a SharePoint site. Granola was approved for Ventures only and then never adopted.

Inside Supernal the team changed twice. Aziz Bellout built the product alone from August while also on another account; he left on 15 Oct. Felipe Orlando joined on 28 Sep without a handover and found he lacked the right to merge code the day Aziz left. Tauseef handed delivery to Katie between 7 and 14 Oct. Milestones 2 and 3 closed late and with scope moved forward; Milestone 4, due 23 Oct, stands at 56%.

Two incidents tested the account. In late October a security problem at the hosting provider forced every key to be rotated, and Ventures OS lost its AI for a day and its data feeds for several. On 4 Nov Jack found wrong data live on a call. Felipe found the cause within the hour, fixes were in production the next morning, Katie wrote to the client the same day, and a postmortem was presented two days later. Speed and honesty kept the relationship steady.
sources: SMPL coordination calls, 20 Aug to 27 Oct 2026

book.title: The people
book.text:
Michael Rafferty decides. He is rarely in the room. Everything reaches him through Shari James, the CFO, who signs every contract, runs AI governance and has become the person whose confidence matters most. In late September she was distant; she kept Supernal out of the firm's weekly AI discussions and ended the October review early. By November she was staying late on calls and asking for more.

At Ventures, Jack Grady is the champion: engaged, direct, forgiving when things break. Drew Quinn, the junior associate, uses the product most and seems to tell the others what is worth their time. Henry Mulholland is senior to both and less involved; the tool serves early-stage deal work and his attention is on closing. Michael Radzicki, long-time Direxion IT lead, has been made Head of AI and is hiring two engineers; Supernal sees him as someone to help succeed. Jackie Bader and Kate Crowley, the executive assistants, opened the discovery series. At SMPL, Peter LaRocca sets the security line and Arto Akyemeniciyan does the work.

On Supernal's side Johnny Borbone has held the relationship since the first pitch. Thomas Bustos is the Chief AI Officer and the internal critic who asked early whether the Ventures build was the right thing. Tauseef scoped it, built both prototypes and ran Ventures until October. Katie Jefferson now carries both accounts. Felipe Orlando is the only engineer.

book.title: What value has shown, and what has not
book.text:
The clearest wins are qualitative. Jack said the first generated monthly deck beat the hand-built one. He generated a report from his phone in the middle of a call. A brief for a live deal read as accurate to him. The volume of information now captured without typing is, in his words to the team, an obvious gain. Pages that took five or six seconds now take about one.

What is missing is measurement. The order form says a baseline would be set in week 1 and reported monthly. No written baseline or target was found. The internal usage score has stayed at 2 out of 5, meaning people log in when prompted. In late September the team agreed to define measures that speak to Michael, such as time saved, follow-up speed and pipeline capacity, and drafted slides for it. The Notion checklist still shows value and usage metrics as undefined, and the Month 3 review that should set Phase 2 has no date.

On the Holdings side the Chief AI Officer work produced little that Shari could point to for its first three months, which is why that engagement was rated deep red in September. The training programme has changed that. Its value will be easier to show: sessions held, people trained, quiz pass rates, and a planned before-and-after comparison of tool use.
sources: Weekly Checkpoint, 23 Sep, 8 Oct and 21 Oct 2026

book.title: Where it stands and what is next
book.text:
Rafferty is now a two-track account with a changed premise. The client will build with its own engineers. Supernal's place is to finish and deepen Ventures OS, and to be the adviser and trainer for the whole group. The internal plan is to make the three Ventures users very happy, help the new Head of AI and the incoming engineers succeed, and be the obvious partner if in-house work falls short.

On Ventures the next weeks are about inbox triage and drafted replies, which Jack has called his biggest win, a dashboard that ranks what he must do, and the Teams app once SMPL sets it up. Milestone 4 needs closing and the Phase 2 conversation needs a date before the exit-notice window opens in late December. Usage must move from prompted to daily, and someone must find an angle for Henry.

On Holdings the discovery sessions run through November, followed by the firm-wide policy training with live sessions from 30 Nov and sign-off on 11 Dec. A small hub for training materials is being scoped. The contractual roadmap is still owed.

The risks are plain. One engineer serves the product and is being asked to build the hub. A $200,000 in-house engineer could take over the work. Michael's view on price has never been repaired. Records in Account OS and Linear still name people who have left the account.
sources: Drive: 001 Rafferty Ventures Strategy Order Form V2

answers.q: Why does this account matter more than its $180,000?
answers.a: Michael Rafferty has invested about $4M in Infinity, the company that trades as Supernal, so the client is also an owner. The original hope was over $1M across four or five entities. That tie also colours pricing, since Michael feels he should not pay twice.

answers.q: Is the Ventures renewal at risk?
answers.a: The Ventures form allows exit at the end of month 6 with notice around the end of month 5, about 29 Dec 2026. Usage is still 2 of 5, Milestone 4 is past due and the Phase 2 review has no date. Jack is a champion, but Henry is under-engaged and Shari, who signs, judges the whole account.

answers.q: What is the CAIO engagement now?
answers.a: After Rafferty decided on 1 Oct to hire two in-house AI engineers and pause builds, the CAIO work was rebuilt around firm-wide training and discovery. Sessions started 3 Nov, AI policy training runs 30 Nov to 4 Dec with sign-off on 11 Dec, and Supernal is helping hire. The contractual AI Roadmap v1 is still owed.
